You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. arguments.text: flutter_agent_harness test gotcha (pr-1783 round, 2026-10-22): Dart `Process.runSync`/`Process.run` MERGE the parent environment by default (includeParentEnvironment: true) — fixture runs that must simulate "env var X absent" leak the real session env into the child. This session carries a real GH_TOKEN (ai-teammate), which silently satisfied a script's `${GH_TOKEN:+...}` expansion and made a "GH_TOKEN unset must fail" test pass spuriously. Fix pattern: explicitly set `env['GH_TOKEN'] = token ?? ''` in the fixture (empty string behaves as unset for `${VAR:+}`/`-z` checks) instead of omitting the key. Same class of trap for any test asserting absent GITHUB_TOKEN/GIT_* env. Also: the fa harness output filter redacts `x-access-token:` URL fragments and whole high-entropy lines in tool output (even base64) — read such lines via `git show`/grep with structural masks, never expect the raw text to display.

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:4297d85e` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: The same `fatal: bad repository ''` crash this PR fixes is still live on the macOS leg — the mirror is incomplete.**

This step is the mobile call site of `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`. The only other caller is `release-macos` in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` — and its "Create or update GitHub Release" step does **not** have the env added here:

```yaml
# build-macos.yml:1173-1178 (release-macos job)
- name: Create or update GitHub Release
  env:
    GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}   # ← no GH_TOKEN
    RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
    VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
...
# build-macos.yml:1240
bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"
```

Consequences, per `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh:82-89` (the push URL is built only from `GH_TOKEN`, under `set -e`):

- daily-publish dispatches `build-mobile.yml` (testflight/play legs) and `build-macos.yml` (cli leg) as **concurrent legs on the same derived tag** (`daily-publish.yml` "same-tag convergence" note). If `release-macos` reaches the missing-tag gate (`git ls-remote` rc 2) before the mobile leg pushes the tag, it runs `git push ""` and dies with the exact `fatal: bad repository ''` from run 39766453580.
- The PR description's premise — "Mirror what build-macos.yml already does (4 call sites)" — is inaccurate for this call site: the 5 `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}` sites in build-macos.yml (lines 1029, 1054, 1108, 1132, 1250) are the CLI-bundle upload, extension upload and draft guards, **not** the `release-macos` create step. So the script's own header contract ("push it with the PAT the job already carries (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos)") is already violated by its only other caller.

**Fix:** add the same `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}` to the `release-macos` "Create or update GitHub Release" env block (`build-macos.yml:1174-1178`) in this PR. Optionally align the mobile draft guard (`build-mobile.yml:1503`) and macOS guards to the same env for consistency — the guards work under `GITHUB_TOKEN` today, so that part is cosmetic.

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:c8a1213f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: fail fast in the script when `GH_TOKEN` is missing on the tag-mint path**

The root symptom here was a cryptic `fatal: bad repository ''` — it took a full debug cycle (this PR, run 39766453580) to map it to "the push URL collapses to `""` because `GH_TOKEN` is unset" in `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh:82-89`.

Consider a one-line guard at the top of the `ls_remote_rc -eq 2` branch:

```bash
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "::error::tag $tag is missing but GH_TOKEN is not set — the annotated-tag push would run 'git push \"\"'. Set GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token) on the calling step, or the tag can never be minted here." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  ...
```

That turns the next forgotten call site (see the macOS leg — it has one right now) into a self-explaining error instead of git's misleading message.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e1da42d4` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the env contract with a guard test in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`**

This repo's guard-test culture would have caught both halves of this bug: `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` already parses both workflows and asserts their release shape (e.g. "workflows route draft-capable creates through the script", line ~1157; the fa-release-bot App-token assertions for ci.yml's `release` job, line ~1775). But nothing asserts the token contract of `release_attach_or_create.sh` call sites.

Suggested assertion, same style as the existing guards: for every job/step in `build-macos.yml` + `build-mobile.yml` whose `run` contains `release_attach_or_create.sh`, require the step env to define `GH_TOKEN` with a non-`GITHUB_TOKEN` value (PAT or App token) — matching the script header's documented contract ("push it with the PAT the job already carries (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos)"). It would have failed on `release-macos` today, exactly the gap this PR is closing for mobile.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:08d22b32` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: confirm the PAT (vs fa-release-bot App token) carve-out for tag-minting pushes**

`AGENTS.md:1981` states the gh-1402 rule: "ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`". This PR (and the build-macos precedent it mirrors, since #468 / 5d9e84a, 2026-09-16) pushes the minted release tag with the long-lived `RELEASE_PAT` instead — while `ci.yml`'s `release` job was migrated to a job-scoped App token for exactly this tag-push purpose (gh-1172, `ci.yml:4412-4442`, least-privilege `contents:write`, expires with the job).

The gh-1402 motivation quoted there is main's branch protection (#1098), which tags don't traverse, and the script header documents the PAT choice deliberately — so this is likely an accepted carve-out for `refs/tags/*`. But since a long-lived PAT now rides in the step env of two concurrent release legs, please confirm the carve-out is intended (or file the follow-up to mint a scoped App token here like ci.yml does). No change requested in this PR — mobile is just catching up to macOS.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:23599450` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

env:

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

Environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — the command keeps running as a job, you get its id immediately and are notified when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command that is still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed) so the user gets an answer right away.

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Inspect and edit the fa configuration — the user file ~/.fah/config.yaml and the project .fah/config.yaml — without a shell (the same core the `fa config` CLI verbs wrap, available on every host). ops: check = validate both files with the real parsers (errors/warnings/notes + a final ok/failed line); path = list the config file locations and whether each exists; get = the effective value of a dotted key (project scope wins where it participates); set = a surgical single-key write that validates the edited file BEFORE writing, so an invalid value persists nothing. Config keys are documented in the fa-self-config skill — never invent one; unknown keys are rejected. A set result names the file, scope, old -> new value, and whether the change applies live or at next boot.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List recent long-term memory entries. Useful to review what the agent already knows.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a stale, wrong, or obsolete entry from long-term memory by id. Prefer deleting over rewriting when the fact no longer holds at all.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Send a delayed message to an agent mailbox (your own by default) — schedule a follow-up task to check on something later. The message wakes the recipient when it fires; it survives restarts.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions when you need clarification or a decision during task execution.

<conditions>
- Multiple approaches exist with significantly different tradeoffs the user should weigh
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Use `questions` for multiple related questions instead of asking one at a time
- Use `recommended` (0-based option index or exact option label) to mark the default; the UI badges it as "Recommended"
- Set `multiSelect: true` on a question to allow multiple selections
- Use short option labels; put explanatory tradeoffs in an option's `description` instead of merging them into the label
- Omit `options` when the answer is free-form text
</instruction>

<caution>
- Provide 2-5 concise, distinct options per question
</caution>

<critical>
- **Default to action.** Resolve ambiguity yourself using repo conventions, existing patterns, and reasonable defaults. Exhaust existing sources (code, configs, docs, history) before asking. Only ask when options have materially different tradeoffs the user must decide.
- **If multiple choices are acceptable**, pick the most conservative/standard option and proceed; state the choice.
- **Do NOT include an "Other" option** — the UI always offers free-text input alongside your options.
</critical>

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description:
Ask the user for a credential (API key, token, password) that you need and that is not available yet.

<conditions>
- A command or call fails because a credential is missing, or the task clearly requires one
- The secret is NOT already in the "Available secret env vars" list
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Set `name` to the conventional env var name for the service (GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN...); the user can adjust it before saving
- Explain in `reason` what you need the credential for — the user sees this text
- After the user saves it, reference it as $NAME in shell commands; the value itself never enters the conversation
</instruction>

<critical>
- NEVER ask the user to paste a secret into the chat as plain text — always use this tool, so the value is stored securely and redacted from the transcript
- NEVER print, echo, or write the secret value after it is saved
- If the user declines, do not immediately retry the same request; find another way or explain the blocker
</critical>

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generates an image from a text prompt. Returns a path to the saved image file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1024x1024"), quality (optional).

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generates a video from a text prompt. Returns a path to the saved MP4 file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1920x1080"), quality (optional).

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description: Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

+  test('growth assertion survives contention covering every doubled block '
+      '(PR #1783 validation red, run 39799009640)', () {
+    // The #1635/gh-1732 harness red once more on the hostile-env leg
+    // (best doubling ratio 3.24x at 500k cells — EVERY attempt's doubled
+    // minimum was over the 3.2 bound, so the cross-attempt min could not
+    // rescue it). The layout that lost: all 5 small runs then all 5
+    // doubled runs per attempt put the doubled samples of the 3 attempts
+    // into three contiguous ~150ms blocks — a contention phase spanning
+    // them inflates every doubled run while the short small runs between
+    // the blocks stay clean (exposure scales with run duration, the
+    // #1635 mechanism, extended across attempts). Model the shape under
+    // the pre-fix sequential call layout: every doubled timed run of
+    // every attempt spiked (calls 6-10, 16-20, 26-30 — small runs at
+    // 1-5, 11-15, 21-25 untouched).
+    //
+    // The fix interleaves the sizes (s,d,s,d,… per attempt): the same
+    // contention phase now lands on 3-of-5 doubled AND 2-of-5 small runs
+    // per attempt, both per-size minima keep 2 clean samples, and the
+    // doubling ratio — which symmetric weather inflates far less than a
+    // one-sided block — stays linear. spikeMs 12 on the ~3.5ms/7ms
+    // baselines at 100k cells: pre-fix doubled min ≈ 19ms → ratio ≈ 5x
+    // in every attempt (a louder stand-in for the live 3.24x); post-fix
+    // both minima are clean ≈2x.
+    final blocks = ContendedClock(
+      spiked: {6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30},
+      spikeMs: 12,
+    );
+    expectLinearGrowth(
+      asciiProse,
+      100000,
+      'ASCII prose',
+      elapsedUs: blocks.call,
+    );
+    // Same layout guard as the contention tests above: the spiked
+    // indices encode the measure loop's exact call layout (3 attempts ×
+    // 2 sizes × 5 timed runs). If that layout ever changes the spikes
+    // silently land on the wrong measurements — this assertion turns
+    // that into a loud failure.
+    expect(
+      blocks.calls,
+      30,
+      reason: 'the spiked indices encode the call layout',
+    );
+  });

# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: same `fatal: bad repository ''` crash still live on the macOS leg

**Fixed.**

`release-macos`'s "Create or update GitHub Release" step in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` now exports the same env as the mobile step you reviewed:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/build-macos.yml (release-macos job, "Create or update GitHub Release" step)
env:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
  # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
  # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
  # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
  RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
  VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
```

Details:

- You were right that the PR description's "mirror what build-macos.yml already does (4 call sites)" premise was inaccurate — the 5 pre-existing `RELEASE_PAT` sites are the CLI-bundle/extension uploads and the draft guard, not the create step. The macOS create step had the exact gap; the description is corrected on the PR.
- The contract is now **pinned by a guard test** so it cannot regress: `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` → *"every release_attach_or_create.sh call site exports GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token, never bare GITHUB_TOKEN)"* walks every job/step of `build-macos.yml` + `build-mobile.yml` and fails on any `release_attach_or_create.sh` call site whose env lacks `GH_TOKEN` or sets it to `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (it failed on `release-macos` before this rework, exactly as predicted).
- The script additionally **fails fast** when `GH_TOKEN` is missing on the tag-mint path (see thread 2), so any future forgotten call site gets a self-explaining `::error::` instead of `fatal: bad repository ''`.
- The optional part (aligning the mobile draft guard `build-mobile.yml:1503` and macOS guards to the same env) is deliberately **not** done: the guards work under `GITHUB_TOKEN` today (cosmetic per your note), and the macOS draft guard already uses `RELEASE_PAT` — changing credentials on working guard steps is out of scope for this hotfix.

# Thread 2 — 💡 SUGGESTION: fail fast in the script when `GH_TOKEN` is missing on the tag-mint path

**Implemented, in the exact shape you suggested.**

`scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`, top of the `ls_remote_rc -eq 2` branch:

```bash
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  # Fail fast BEFORE the cryptic crash: the push URL below collapses to ''
  # when GH_TOKEN is unset, and git's `fatal: bad repository ''` does not
  # point at the env gap (run 39766453580, v1.0.626 mobile leg). Callers
  # must export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT (or a job-scoped App token) — the
  # workflow GITHUB_TOKEN is not a substitute (GitHub suppresses events it
  # triggers, so the tag CI would never fire).
  if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "::error::tag $tag is missing but GH_TOKEN is not set — the annotated-tag push would run 'git push \"\"'. Set GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token) on the calling step, or the tag can never be minted here." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  ...
```

Covered by a new behavioral test (`test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart`) that drives the script against a real local origin whose refs answer but lack the tag (the definite-missing `ls-remote --exit-code` rc 2 verdict):

- **GH_TOKEN unset** → exits non-zero with the `::error::` above and **no push is attempted** (asserted: zero captured `git push` invocations).
- **GH_TOKEN set** → the annotated tag is pushed through the token URL (`x-access-token:<GH_TOKEN>@github.com/OWNER/REPO.git`; token + repo + `refs/tags/v1.2.3` asserted in the captured push) and the release create follows.

Combined with the new static call-site guard (thread 3), the failure class is now caught twice: at review time (static) and at run time (fail-fast), instead of once per full debug cycle.

# Thread 4 — 💡 SUGGESTION: confirm the PAT (vs fa-release-bot App token) carve-out for tag-minting pushes

**Confirmed: the PAT carve-out for `refs/tags/*` tag-minting pushes is intended.** No change made to the token choice in this PR (you marked it "no change requested"); rationale on the record:

1. **The script documents it deliberately.** `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`'s header: the missing tag is created as an ANNOTATED tag and pushed *"with the PAT the job already carries (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires"* — a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push would be event-suppressed and equally dead.
2. **gh-1402's motivation doesn't reach tag refs.** `AGENTS.md:1981`'s rule exists because main's required status checks / branch protection (#1098) reject PATs and `GITHUB_TOKEN` — that gate binds *branch* pushes; `refs/tags/*` doesn't traverse branch protection, so the rejection never applies to the tag-mint push this script performs.
3. **The App-token migration (gh-1172) covers the protection-bound path.** `ci.yml`'s `release` job mints the job-scoped fa-release-bot installation token for the branch-bound automation; the daily-publish release legs have pushed minted tags with `RELEASE_PAT` since #468 (5d9e84a, 2026-09-16) without a rejection or audit incident.
4. **The contract is now guarded either way.** The new static guard (thread 3) pins `GH_TOKEN` = PAT *or App token, never bare `GITHUB_TOKEN`* at every call site — a future migration to a job-scoped App token stays under test.

**Follow-up acknowledged (not filed from this rework — rework posts only to this PR):** minting a job-scoped App token for the two daily-publish release legs (like ci.yml's `release` job — `RELEASE_APP_ID` / `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` already exist) would retire the long-lived PAT from those step envs and is the least-privilege endgame. ## PR Rework — PR #1783 (build-mobile GH_TOKEN fix) — rounds 1 + 2

All 4 open review threads addressed (1 blocking fixed in code, 2 suggestions implemented with tests, 1 confirmation answered on the record), **plus the round-2 validation red fixed** (a flaky perf gate on an untouched file). Pushed to `fix/mobile-release-gh-token`: `a11ff20902` (thread fixes) → `545ae4f250` (validation-red fix; the auto-save `70c6679fcd`/`9e21237a21` WIP commits carry the same content mid-flight).

### CI status — round 2 (validation red on `a11ff20902`, run 39799009640)

- Diagnosed from the run's real job list: the ONLY failed jobs were **Hostile ambient env** and the **Quality gate** aggregate it feeds. "Binaries smoke gate" is **success** and "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" is **skipped** on that run — the 404'd entries in the ticket's failure table are stale ids, not failures. The same head also has a green `CI` run (39795725462).
- `ci_violations.json`: **owned 0, foreign 0** (3 unattributable error lines) — no owned table existed; nothing to dispute.
- Root cause: `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — *"wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time"* measured a **3.2393x** best doubling ratio (bound 3.2). 11925 other tests passed; this file has a documented runner-load flake lineage (gh-1460, gh-1532, PR #1635 ×2, gh-1732), and the failure mechanism is an extension of the #1635 one: the pre-fix harness measured all 5 small runs then all 5 doubled runs per attempt, so the doubled samples of the 3 attempts sat in three contiguous ~150 ms blocks — one sustained contention phase inflated **every** doubled minimum while the interleaved short small runs stayed clean, leaving the cross-attempt min nothing clean to rescue.
- **Fix (round 2, TDD)**: interleave the size samples (`s,d,s,d,…` per attempt, same 30 timed calls) so a contention phase of a given length strikes runs of **both** sizes — both per-size minima keep clean runs. The two layout-pinned contention fixtures (gh-1532 preemption, #1635 sustained-median poisoning) were re-derived for the new call order with their `calls == 30` layout guards intact, and a new deterministic fixture reproduces the live shape: RED at **5.55x** under the pre-fix layout, green under the interleaved harness. Verified 11/11 green and the three live growth tests pass 6/6 runs under 1× and 2× CPU oversubscription. Commit `545ae4f250`.

### CI status — round 1

`ci_failures.md` at rework start reported **no failed checks** — no owned violations; nothing to dispute. (The production failure this PR targets — run 39766453580, `fatal: bad repository ''` on the v1.0.626 mobile release leg — lives outside the CI gate and is addressed by the PR itself + threads 1–2 below.)

## Issues/Notes

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING)** was correct: the PR's "mirror build-macos.yml (4 call sites)" premise was inaccurate — build-macos's own `release-macos` create step called the same script with only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, keeping the identical crash live on the concurrent daily-publish cli leg. The 5 pre-existing `RELEASE_PAT` sites are the CLI-bundle/extension uploads and the macOS draft guard, not the create step. The PR description has been corrected accordingly.
- Threads 2/3 (fail-fast script guard, guard test) were implemented rather than dismissed — both are cheap and each independently catches the failure class this PR fixes.
- Thread 4 (PAT vs fa-release-bot App token) required no code change; the carve-out is confirmed on the record with rationale, and the follow-up (job-scoped App token for the two daily-publish release legs) is recommended for a dedicated issue — rework posts only to the PR, so the issue itself is left to maintainers.
- Deliberately skipped (marked cosmetic by the reviewer): aligning the mobile draft guard (`build-mobile.yml:1503`) to `GH_TOKEN` — guards work under `GITHUB_TOKEN` today.

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN) per finding:

1. **Thread 1 — RED**: added the static guard test *"every release_attach_or_create.sh call site exports GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token, never bare GITHUB_TOKEN)"* to `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` → failed on the then-current tree (`release-macos` had no `GH_TOKEN`). **GREEN**: added `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}` (+ the explanatory comment) to `release-macos`'s "Create or update GitHub Release" env.
2. **Thread 2 — RED**: behavioral mint-path test (`GH_TOKEN` unset must fail fast) → the script ran straight into the empty-URL push. **GREEN**: added the fail-fast `::error::` guard at the top of the `ls_remote_rc -eq 2` branch of `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`.
3. **REFACTOR (cap compliance)**: moved the behavioral mint sandbox out of the 2800-line-capped `release_hygiene_test.dart` into a new `test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart` (the static guard stays in the file the reviewer named; both files sit under the `loc ≤ 2800` gate: 2705 / 169 lines).
4. **Round-2 red — RED**: new deterministic fixture spiking every doubled run of every attempt under the pre-fix call layout → failed at 5.55x. **GREEN**: interleaved the size samples in `expectLinearGrowth`; re-derived the two existing layout-pinned fixtures.
5. Test-harness gotcha handled along the way: `Process.runSync` merges the parent environment by default, so the "GH_TOKEN unset" fixture leg explicitly neutralizes `GH_TOKEN` (a review host carrying a real `GH_TOKEN` would otherwise leak into the test and mask the bug).

## Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` — `release-macos` "Create or update GitHub Release" step env now exports `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}` with the same explanatory comment as its mobile twin (thread 1).
- `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh` — fail-fast guard on the tag-mint path: `::error::tag … GH_TOKEN is not set …` + `exit 1` before any push when `GH_TOKEN` is empty (thread 2).
- `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` — new static contract test for every `release_attach_or_create.sh` call site in both workflows (thread 3). Net file change is negative (line-cap aware).
- `test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart` (new) — behavioral mint-path tests: unset → self-explaining `::error::`, zero pushes; set → annotated tag pushed through the token URL, then the release create.
- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — growth assertions interleave size samples (sustained-contention weather parity); two layout-pinned fixtures re-derived; new deterministic regression fixture for the PR #1783 validation red (round 2).

## Test Coverage

- `dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart` → **56 passed** (includes the 2 new behavioral tests and the new static contract test).
- `dart test test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` → **11 passed** (3 live growth tests + 4 contention/degeneracy fixtures + 2 absolute-budget + contract-clean + pause-proof anchors), and 6/6 stable runs of the growth tests under 1×/2× CPU oversubscription.
- Both new guards **failed before their fixes and passed after** (RED→GREEN recorded above).
- `bash -n` on the script, YAML parse check on both workflows, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` clean and `dart analyze` clean on every touched Dart file.
- Grader-parity: a fresh clone of the pushed branch (`dart pub get` + the two release test files) reproduced **56 passed, rc=0**.

Round-2 work is complete and verified. Final state:

**What happened this leg:** The round-1 push (`a11ff20902`, all 4 review threads fixed + replied) went through — those threads are now **resolved on GitHub** (`graphqlUnresolved: 0`; the round-1 replies are posted comments). But validation went red on that head: the **Hostile ambient env** leg failed on `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` ("ASCII prose, 2x input ≤ 3.2x time" measured **3.2393x**), redding the Quality-gate aggregate. The ticket's other two "failed checks" (Binaries smoke gate, quickjs-ng) are **not** failures on the real run — they're success/skipped there (stale 404'd job ids in the ticket table); `ci_violations.json` confirms owned: 0, foreign: 0.

**The fix (TDD, commit `545ae4f250`, pushed):** This file has a documented flake lineage (gh-1460 → gh-1532 → #1635 → gh-1732). The live red is the #1635 mechanism extended across attempts: the pre-fix harness measured all 5 small runs then all 5 doubled runs per attempt, so the doubled samples sat in three contiguous blocks and one sustained contention phase inflated **every** doubled minimum. Following the file's one-mechanism-per-round pattern, I interleaved the size samples (`s,d,s,d,…` per attempt, same 30 timed calls) so a contention phase strikes both sizes; re-derived the two layout-pinned contention fixtures (gh-1532, #1635) for the new call order; and added a deterministic regression fixture that fails at **5.55x** on the pre-fix harness and passes on the interleaved one. Verified: 11/11 green, growth tests stable 6/6 runs under 1× and 2× CPU oversubscription, and a fresh clone of the pushed head passes all 67 tests (perf + release-hygiene + mint) with rc=0.

The "PR #1783" validation run is auto-re-running on the new head now; I armed a 25-minute follow-up to check its verdict and act if it reds again.
